That on 10.05.2024 at about 17-30 hours, Nagesh Murthy A.R. was proceeding in Bajaj Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-K-7969 as a pillion rider, of which his son Prashanth was the rider and they were proceeding from Bellur towards Anakanahalli and when they reached Bellur - Dabbeghatta road, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya Dist, at that time the rider of said vehicle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, due to the impact, the rider lost control over the vehicle, result of which the vehicle got skidded at turning point result of which Nagesh Murthy fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Sparsh Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 10-05-2024 to 15-05- 2024.

Again he was shifted to Adichunchanagiri Hospital, thereafter he was shifted to KIMS Hospital,
Bengaluru wherein he was died on 20-05-2024 during the course of treatment.
So far, the petitioners have spent Rs.15,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment.
They have also spent more than Rs.1,50,000/- towards funeral and obsequies ceremony of the deceased.
3. Prior to the accident, A.R. Nagesh Murthy was hale and healthy.
He was aged about 59 years.
He was doing Agriculture and Milk vending work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden death of deceased, petitioners have suffered from pain and mental agony and other pecuniary and non-pecuniary damages.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 - the owner of Bajaj Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-K-7969 has remained absent.
Hence, he was placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent No.2 / the insurer of Bajaj Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-K-7969 has filed written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.

The respondent no.2 has contended that the deceased was the rider of the insured vehicle and rider is not covered by the policy issued by Nagarathna A vs Praveen Kumar H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145341571/
2 respondent no.2 and the deceased/rider was not holding a valid and effective driving license and he was not wearing helmet.

The respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the fact of the son of Nagesh Murthy riding the motorcycle and Nagesh Murthy traveling in the said vehicle as pillion rider and thereby taken the defence that A.R Nagesh Murthy being the rider of the Insurer vehicle, policy was not covered because Nagesh Murthy being the rider steps in to the shoes of the insured, hence,
submitted to dismiss the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Nagesh Murthy A.R., died on account of road traffic accident on 10.05.2024 at about 17.30 hours, near Dasanakere Cross, Bellur- Dabbeghatta Road, Belluru Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of Bajaj Pulsar Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54- K-7969?
2.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3
. What order or Award ?
7. The petitioner No.1 got examined herself as Pw1 and two witnesses are examined as PW.2 and PW.3 and got marked documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P24.

On the other hand, the respondent no.2 got examined Auto Driver by name Babu stated to be the eye witness as Rw.1 and examined the Investigating agency as RW.2 and got marked document as Ex.R1 to Ex.R5.
Dr. Shivanna -Casualty Medical officer at Adichunchanagiri Medical College is examined as RW.3 and got marked documents at Ex.R6 and Ex.R7.

8. Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.
9.

My findings on the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No. 1 - In the Negative Issue No. 2 - Does not survive for consideration Issue No. 3 - As per final Order, for the following:-
REASONS 10. Issues No.1:-

Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, Nagesh Murthy A.R. (hereinafter called the deceased) was proceeding in Bajaj Pulsar Motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54/K-7969 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) as a pillion rider, of which Nagarathna A vs Praveen Kumar H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145341571/
3 his son Prashanth was the rider and they were proceeding from Bellur towards Anakanahalli and when they reached Bellur - Dabbeghatta road, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya Dist, at that time the rider of offending vehicle rode the same in a rash and negligent manner, due to the impact, the rider lost control over the vehicle, result of which the vehicle got skid at turning, result of which deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

11. In order to prove the petition averments, petitioner no.1 who is the wife of deceased got examined herself as Pw1 and produced in all 16 documents, among them Ex.P1 to Ex.P10 are the police documents (i.e,) F.I.R with complaint, further statement of the complainant and requisition,
Crime detailed form with Spot sketch, seizure mahazar, Notice U/sec.133 of IMV Act and reply to said notice, Inquest report, PM report, Charge sheet, Police intimation MLC and Dama Summary are the material documents to prove the present issue.

12. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri.Krishna Murthy, case has been registered against the rider of offending vehicle in Crime No.79/2024 by Bellur Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279 and 337 IPC.
The Investigation officer after investigation has filed charge sheet against the rider of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of IPC.

13. The respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the contention taken by the petitioners as to the deceased traveling in the offending vehicle as pillion rider and the son of the deceased riding the offending vehicle as rider and submitted that since the accident in question has occurred due to the own negligence of the deceased, in order to get compensation, the son of the deceased was falsely implicated as the rider of the offending vehicle.

In order to substantiate the said contention, the respondent no.2 has mainly relied upon the delay in lodging the complaint, not taking treatment by the son of the deceased who stated to be the rider of the said vehicle, the evidence of the RW.2 and the corrections made in the MLC register at Ex.P18.
14.
In the light of the serious objection raised by the respondent no.2, if the materials placed on record is perused, the accident in question has occurred on 10- 05-2024 at about 17-30 hours.
The complaint came to be lodged on 14-05-2024 at about 11-30 pm.
There is delay of 4 days in lodging the complaint.
The complaint is lodged by one Krishana Murthy who is the relative of the deceased.
In the complaint and in the FIR the reason for delay has been explained stating that since the complainant was in the hospital with the patient, there was delay in lodging the complaint.
In the complaint it is stated that the son of the deceased by name Prashanth was riding the offending vehicle and due to the accident Prashanth has also sustained injuries.
Admittedly, the petitioners have not produced any document to prove that Prashanth has sustained any injuries and he has taken treatment from any of the hospital.
It is deposed by PW.1 that her son Prashanth has also taken treatment but the medical documents of her son was lost.

If really Prashanth had taken treatment in any of the hospital and if really medical documents of Prashanth was lost, the petitioners could have collected the medical documents from the hospital in which Prashanth stated to have taken treatment.
But no such steps has been taken by the petitioners to prove that due to the accident Prashanth had also sustained injuries.

When as per the case of petitioners, the deceased who was the pillion rider had succumbed to the injuries due to the accident and when the gravity of Nagarathna A vs Praveen Kumar H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145341571/
4 the accident is to such an extent that it has taken away the life of deceased, under such circumstances if really Prashanth was riding the vehicle he had to sustain some injuries and he had to take treatment for the injuries sustained by him.

sentences.text:
The respondent no.2 has examined the CMO,
Adichunchangiri Medical College as RW.3 wherein deceased had taken treatment.

As per the evidence of RW.1 who stated to be the eye witness, the injured Nagesh Murthy was shifted to the hospital till a little distance through his Autorickshaw and thereafter the injured Nagesh Murthy was shifted from his vehicle to the ambulance.
The RW.1 nowhere has stated the injury if any sustained by Prashanth and shifting Prashanth along with the deceased to the hospital in the said ambulance.
Through out the evidence, the RW.1 has stated only about one injured person ie., of deceased and there is no whisper about the injury sustained by Prashanth.
RW.3 - Dr. Shivanna has deposed that Prashanth has not taken any treatment in their hospital.
When it was suggested to the RW.3 that the injured Nagesh Murthy was accompanied by RW.1 in the ambulance but not Prashanth, the RW.3 has not denied the same.

As per the evidence of RW.3, at the time of injured Nagesh Murthy was shifted to the hospital he was in a position to give the statement and deceased has not given any statement before the hospital about his traveling in the offending vehicle as pillion rider.
If MLC record is perused, wherein the name of RW.1 finds place as person who brought the injured Nagesh Murthy to the hospital.
It is true that even the name of Prashanth finds place in the MLC.
If really Prashanth had brought his father to the hospital then the name of RW.1 would not have been mentioned in the MLC.
It clearly reveals that it is after the deceased was brought to the hospital by RW.1 in ambulance, the son of deceased came to the hospital.

If really Prashanth was riding the motorcycle he would have sustained injuries and he would have taken treatment in the very same hospital and in the event if Prashanth had not sustained any injury, he could have shifted his father to the hospital.

Further when petitioners have not produced any document to prove that Prashanth too has sustained injuries and when Prashanth was in the hospital as it is evident from MLC register, the complainant or Prashanth or the petitioners could have lodged complaint on the date of accident itself or in the next date of the accident.
Hence the reason assigned by complainant stating that since he was in the hospital, he could not lodge the complaint in time can not be accepted.
15. The respondent no.2 has examined its investigating agency as RW.2.

The RW.2 has deposed about his being appointed as Investigator to investigate the accident case by collecting documents and recording the statement of the petitioners, witness, owner/driver of the offending vehicle etc.,
RW.2 has produced letter of authorization given to him to investigate the case on behalf of respondent no.2 and produced FSL report with CD.
The respondent no.2 has displayed the CD in the open court through laptop.
In the video clippings, the statement of the RW.1 Babu was recorded so also the statement of Byregowda who is the mahazar witness to the accident.

RW.1 in his statement has stated that on the date of accident deceased alone was traveling in the offending vehicle and he was riding the offending vehicle and at the curve, the said vehicle skidded and rider sustained injuries.
In the said record the RW.1 has stated that he has accompanied the injured Nagesh Murthy to the hospital and his son Prashanth came to the hospital later on.

Even Byregowda by giving statement has stated that he has not seen the accident but being a mahazar witness he came to know that while Nagesh Murthy was riding the motorcycle as rider, he met with an accident.

As per the evidence of RW.2, he has recorded even the statement of the owner and alleged driver of the offending vehicle so also of the petitioners but since there is no clippings of the statement given by the aforesaid persons they have not produced their video recording.

When RW.2 Nagarathna A vs Praveen Kumar H N on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/145341571/
5 has recorded the statement of petitioners, owner and alleged rider of the offending vehicle in the same device in which the statement of RW.1 and Byregowda was recorded there is no reason to believe that the video clippings of the statement of the petitioners, owner and alleged rider of the offending vehicle was damaged.

entities.text: RW.2 Nagarathna A vs Praveen Kumar H N
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears that petitioners, owner and alleged rider have given statement in support of the averments of the complaint, the respondent no.2 has not produced video clippings of their statement .
It is quite natural that the petitioners, owner and the alleged rider of the offending vehicle being the family members of the deceased may not have given statement against to their own case.
Hence, the respondent no.2 has suppressed their video clippings.
16. If the MLC record produced by the respondent no.2 at Ex.R6 is perused, we can see over writings, deletion and inclusion of certain words.

The MLC records clearly goes to show that at the first instance the history is mentioned as "RTA fall from Two Wheeler Bike on 10-05-2024 at about 5-30 pm., near Dasanakere turning Nagamangala, Mandya District while riding bike and sustained injuries.

Ex.R1 clearly shows that after the word Mandya District the name "Prashanth" was inserted and in between the word "riding the bike" and "sustained injuries", the word "Mr. Nagesh Murthy as a pillion rider due to skid was inserted".

The said over writings, deletion and insertion of words clearly reveals that at the first instance RW.1 has given information to the hospital authorities about Nagesh Murthy sustained injuries on the stated date, time and place due to skid while riding the motorcycle.
Later on in order to get compensation the name of Prashanth was inserted as the rider of motorcycle and deceased as pillion rider.

Hence, even if the evidence of RW.2 and the documents produced by the RW.2 is excluded, based on the evidence of the RW.1 and RW.3 coupled with Ex.R6 and the delay in lodging the complaint and the fact of Prashanth not taking any treatment in the hospital and not shifting his father to the hospital etc., clearly reveals that Prashanth was not at all present at the spot and he was not at all riding the offending vehicle and deceased himself was riding the offending vehicle and due to his own negligence he met with an accident and succumbed to the injuries.

It is because the accident in question has occurred due to the own negligence of the deceased, in order to get compensation, the son of the deceased was implicated at the later stage as the rider of the offending vehicle.
Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the Negative.
17. Issue No.2:- Since the accident in question has occurred due to the own negligence of the deceased, the petitioners are not entitled for compensation.
Hence, issue no.2 is also answered in the negative.
18. Issue No.3:
In the light of the findings given on Issue No.1 and 2, my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby dismissed.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer directly on computer, corrected and then pronounced by me in open court, on this the 3rd day of January 2026.)
